title_vi: Sáu mẫu kiến trúc phần mềm: mỗi mẫu một lợi, một hại, và một phép đo

claims.evidence: Six patterns and their pros and cons from the source body; n-tier, microservices and event-driven statements read from local clones of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at 8e2c239 and the plugin-discovery guide from pypa/packaging.python.org at d1ad4ad; six costs measured by a Python 3.13.16 program on a 4-vCPU virtual machine on 2026-10-19 (three runs). claims.claim_vi: Source: six patterns - layered (distinct roles; quick to build; code can become unorganized without rules), microservices (smaller components; fault tolerant; scale individually; more complex), event-driven (services emit events others may or may not consume; loose coupling; testing is challenging), client-server (clients and servers over a network; real-time services; server can be a single point of failure), plugin-based (core plus independent plugins; good for IDEs; changing the core is difficult), hexagonal (abstraction layer protecting the core, ports and adapters; more development time and learning curve).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft N-tier: a higher layer can use a lower layer, not the reverse; tiers are physically separated and add network latency; a middle tier that only performs basic CRUD adds latency and complexity without meaningful value; testing and monitoring are harder through multiple tiers.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft microservices: independent deployment, fault isolation, independent scaling; challenges include complexity, network congestion and latency, data integrity across services.
claims.verified_by: Read from the same local clone.

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft event-driven: producers are decoupled from consumers and do not know who listens; the style can be unsuitable where strong consistency is needed, because of eventual consistency, and asynchronous debugging is harder.
claims.section: Introduction; When to use this architecture
claims.verified_by: Read from the same local clone.

claims.claim_vi: Python packaging guide: three major approaches to automatic plugin discovery - naming convention, namespace packages, package metadata.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of pypa/packaging.python.org at commit d1ad4ad3d6d6f3a3582e4c6b8a1b6f8284f4cb3b.

claims.claim_vi: Measurements (three runs): forwarding layer adds 0.02-0.05 us per call; in-process call 0.08-0.11 us versus HTTP call 220-292 us on the same machine; synchronous publish adds about 0.02 us per subscriber (0 subscribers 0.13-0.23, 100 subscribers 2.4-2.8 us); queue-and-thread delivery median 51-59 us (p99 333-2220 us); single-threaded HTTP server with a 5 ms handler: 5.8 ms with 1 client, 22.3-22.7 with 4, 33.4-33.5 with 16, threaded 6.1, 6.1-6.4, 8.5-8.6 ms; discovering 100 plugin modules 9.0-10.9 ms and importing them 13.6-17.4 ms; changing the hook signature breaks 100 of 100 plugins (0 with a fallback); hexagonal core with memory adapter 0.20-0.23 us and with sqlite3 adapter (commit each) 890-960 us.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19 (three runs); one machine, toy structures.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung: sáu mẫu một lợi một hại, sáu phép đo, giới hạn.
source_deviations: The source is a picture with six short paragraphs; the lesson keeps the six patterns in order, adds a cross-check column and one small measurement per pattern.
Client-server and hexagonal have no independent reference; the cost of designing a hexagonal system is not measured.
